newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DAVIES CUTS FINGER AHEAD OF U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DAVIES CUTS FINGER AHEAD OF U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN.

text.p: Briton Laura Davies will have to overcome a cut finger and a dodgy putter to keep Sweden's Annika Sorenstam from a three-peat at the U.S. Women's Open, which begins here Thursday.
Davies sliced a big gash in her left index finger while slicing bread at her hotel Tuesday morning.
"I thought I had the sharp side cutting the bread, but I had the blunt side, so I cut my finger with the other side," explained Davies.
She insisted the cut had not hindered her grip, but she was unable to take her glove off to putt during 12 practice holes on the Pumpkin Ridge course Tuesday.
Inconsistent putting is likely to be the biggest obstacle in Davies's quest to add a second U.S. Women's Open to her 1987 title.
"If I can turn around the putting and make a few putts, I'll have a chance, but if you don't hole putts you can't do well," the 33-year-old Davies said.
"That's been holding me back the last few months. I've been hitting some good putts, but I've also been throwing in a few hideous putts as well.
"I've used about eight different putters in the last eight weeks."
Davies was much happier with the rest of her game, particularly her iron play, which she rates as the strongest part of her game.
As the longest hitter in women's golf, however, Davies was disappointed to find the 6,365-yard, par-71 course playing shorter than she had expected.
"I heard it was a long course but it's not that long," she said. "I don't think level par is going to win, because the course is very playable.
"I think if you're four or five under Sunday morning, you're going to have a good squeak at it."
Davies said two-time defending champion Sorenstam is the player to beat.
"If I finish one shot ahead of Annika, I'm probably going to be holding that trophy," she said.
"You've got to do something special to beat her. She's as cool as anybody I've ever seen. The way she's playing is very, very impressive."
